name: How are electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems integrated into a home addition?

mainEntity.name: How are electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems integrated into a home addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Managing utility integration requires checking your existing electrical service panel, heating and cooling capacity, and waste pipe tie-in points. If your current furnace or AC unit cannot support extra square footage, you may need supplemental ductwork or ductless mini-split systems. For bathroom or wet-bar additions, waste and supply lines must tie into main drains properly. At HH Remodeling, our crew frames walls to accommodate mechanical lines and coordinates licensed trade specialists to handle complex electrical and plumbing tie-ins safely.
acceptedAnswer.description: Systems are evaluated during planning to confirm capacity, followed by rough-in work coordinated with licensed trade specialists before wall insulation and drywall.
